chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, all from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The man does not inherit if he kills his child or his parent, but the inheritance belongs to the inheritors of the killer.
ai.seo_question: Does a father inherit from his son if he killed him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of 'gharamah' (deduction of blood money) or exclusion from inheritance, ruling that a killer does not inherit from a direct ascendant or descendant they killed, with the estate passing to the killer's other heirs. This ruling is distinct from general inheritance rules and reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on preventing the unjust enrichment of the killer while maintaining the integrity of the family line. The principle underscores the moral and legal consequence of homicide within the immediate family structure.
